title: Integrate two processor cores on one POWER4 chip
decision: Make the basic POWER4 processor a single chip containing two complete processor cores.
rationale: The paper presents dual-core integration as a way to increase processor density and system throughput while staying within practical chip, power, and packaging limits.
outcome: POWER4 became a dual-core chip and the core building block for POWER4 systems.
weakest_point: The stated rationale wording may be inferred rather than quoted; the paper may not explicitly discuss rejected single-core alternatives.

title: Use an eight-processor MCM building block
decision: Package four dual-core POWER4 chips, with associated cache chips, in a multichip module as the basic eight-processor building block.
rationale: The paper describes the MCM as a way to obtain high processor density and short, fast chip-to-chip interconnects in a scalable building block.
outcome: The MCM provided an eight-core building block from which larger POWER4 systems could be constructed.
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly gives the short-interconnect rationale or simply describes the MCM configuration.

title: Balance clock frequency with instructions-per-cycle
decision: Design for high frequency but keep the pipeline and microarchitecture balanced so that IPC is not sacrificed solely for frequency.
rationale: The paper's design discussion treats frequency as an important lever for performance, but not one to be pursued in isolation from useful work per cycle and system balance.
outcome: The resulting POWER4 microarchitecture combined a wide out-of-order core with a high-frequency design target.
weakest_point: Whether the paper explicitly frames this as a trade-off decision rather than simply describing the chosen pipeline and frequency.

title: Make RAS features pervasive in the POWER4 system
decision: Include error detection, correction, logging, and serviceability mechanisms across caches, buses, memory, and logic.
rationale: The paper presents RAS as necessary for enterprise-class availability, fault containment, and field service in POWER4 systems.
outcome: POWER4 systems include ECC/parity/redundancy/error-handling features intended to reduce failures and downtime.
weakest_point: The exact list of mechanisms and whether the paper uses the term 'pervasive' may be generalized.

title: Provide hardware-coherent shared-memory interconnect for scaling
decision: Use a coherent shared-memory interconnect so multiple POWER4 chips/MCMs can operate as a single SMP system.
rationale: The paper treats hardware coherence and a shared-address-space model as the way to scale processor count while preserving SMP usability.
outcome: POWER4 chips/MCMs can be connected into larger cache-coherent shared-memory systems.
weakest_point: Whether the paper frames this as an explicit design decision or simply describes the coherent interconnect implementation.
